SMTO-GML-0017 — SMTO couldn't find that email in Gmail

GUID: e9cd8cd8-2bee-4f44-8a8f-d939bf1ac4f0
Slug: gmail-message-not-found
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO needed a specific email to reply, forward or change, but couldn't find it. It may have been deleted, or it belongs to a different conversation or account. Nothing was sent or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and check that the email still exists and wasn't deleted or permanently removed. If the email is gone, there is nothing for SMTO to reply to or forward.
  2. Ask SMTO to search for the email again, for example by sender and subject, and then do the reply, forward or change on that result. A fresh search gives SMTO the email's current details instead of an old reference.
  3. If you have more than one Gmail account connected, mention the right one with @ in your request. The email may be in a different account than the one SMTO checked.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the email and shows the reply, forward or change for your approval, and after you approve it, it reports the action as done.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to reuse an old email reference after the email was moved or deleted.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail action could not resolve a selected message: the provider returned 404 for it, a reply's thread_id disagrees with the message's thread, the message is not in the thread used for the reply, or explicit message IDs in a bulk or reply-and-archive selection were not all found.

What this means

  • Reply selection names a message outside the selected thread, supplied thread_id disagrees with provider message ownership, or provider message lookup reports missing. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Reply selection names a message outside the selected thread, supplied thread_id disagrees with provider message ownership, or provider message lookup reports missing.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact account, message ID and thread ownership against live evidence.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._mime maps a get_message 404 or a reply thread_id that differs from the message's threadId to gmail_message_not_found, and build_reply_mime rejects a message_id not in the thread; workflows.select raises it when explicit IDs are missing from get_message_states, and reply_and_archive raises it when the message_id has no state row (app-password accounts raise the same code from the Gateway IMAP path). Re-run gmail.search or gmail.read_thread for the correct account_ref and pass current message IDs (omit thread_id or use the message's own threadId).
  • Refresh live mailbox state and use the intended current message identifier.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Reply/forward preparation uses the intended existing message in its actual thread.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
